We propose a two-phase optimization strategy combining continuous optimization and graph-based rounding to escape local optima
The central idea is to smooth the objective function using LogSumExp (LogSE) penalization and optimize a weighted combination
of all lags to avoid premature convergence. This method preserves the global structure of the original problem while
making it more computationally tractable. The key innovation is the application of simulated annealing to navigate
the complex constraint space (h(x) ∈ [0,1] with ∑h(x)*dx = 1).

2. Mathematical specification:
• Definition: Step function h:[0,2]→[0,1] with n_points samples
• Objective: Minimize C₅ = max_{k} [∫h(x)(1-h(x+k))dx] (with dx=2/n_points)
• Constraints: 0 ≤ h_i ≤ 1 for all i, and Σh_i * dx = 1
• Formulation: We simplify by treating h as a continuous vector and then rounding to [0,1] while maintaining the sum constraint
• Mathematical Objective (LogSE smoothing):
  F(h) = max_{k} [∫h(x)(1-h(x+k))dx] + (1/α)logΣ_{k} exp(α*[G(h,k) - max_k G(h,k)])
where G(h,k) is the normalized correlation for lag k

   C. Simulated annealing:
